So, how is this different from how the Apple Watch currently works?
While most of the stuff on the Apple Watch is run on the phone, Apple doesn't eliminate storage reading and writing completely, do they?

WiFi offloading would be pretty much useless, infrastructure simply uses too much energy to be viable. With BLE I can understand this, although BLE is made for state offloading, not data offloading, but pretty much a wearable only uses states for day to day use anyway. Perfect example is probably the pebble which just pushes states back and forth, and has a battery life of up to 7 days.

Edit: the only thing this will accomplish is that your energy usage will get transferred from your wearable to your mobile device. Seeing Android with the doze function I don't think it's a good idea to keep waking up your phone from doze just to do some minor data storage.

// ==UserScript==
// [@name](/user/name) Replace Text On Webpages
// [@namespace](/user/namespace) [http://userscripts.org/users/23652](http://userscripts.org/users/23652)
// [@description](/user/description) Replaces text on websites. Now supports wildcards in search queries. Won't replace text in certain tags like links and code blocks
// [@include](/user/include) http://*
// [@include](/user/include) https://*
// [@include](/user/include) file://*
// [@exclude](/user/exclude) [http://userscripts.org/scripts/review/](http://userscripts.org/scripts/review/)*
// [@exclude](/user/exclude) [http://userscripts.org/scripts/edit/](http://userscripts.org/scripts/edit/)*
// [@exclude](/user/exclude) [http://userscripts.org/scripts/edit_src/](http://userscripts.org/scripts/edit_src/)*
// [@exclude](/user/exclude) [https://userscripts.org/scripts/review/](https://userscripts.org/scripts/review/)*
// [@exclude](/user/exclude) [https://userscripts.org/scripts/edit/](https://userscripts.org/scripts/edit/)*
// [@exclude](/user/exclude) [https://userscripts.org/scripts/edit_src/](https://userscripts.org/scripts/edit_src/)*
// [@copyright](/user/copyright) JoeSimmons
// [@version](/user/version) 1.1.0
// [@license](/user/license) [http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/3.0/us/](http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/3.0/us/)
// [@downloadURL](/user/downloadurl) [http://userscripts.org/scripts/source/41369.user.js](http://userscripts.org/scripts/source/41369.user.js)
// [@updateURL](/user/updateurl) [http://userscripts.org/scripts/source/41369.meta.js](http://userscripts.org/scripts/source/41369.meta.js)
// ==/UserScript==
(function () {
 'use strict';


 /*
 NOTE: 
 You can use \\* to match actual asterisks instead of using it as a wildcard!
 The examples below show a wildcard in use and a regular asterisk replacement.
 */

 var words = {
 ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////


 // Syntax: 'Search word' : 'Replace word',
 'your a' : 'you\'re a',
 'imo' : 'in my opinion',
 'im\\*o' : 'matching an asterisk, not a wildcard',
 '/\\bD\\b/g' : '[D]',


 ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////
 'reddit':'DONTCLICK',
 'Pao':'DONTCLICK',
 'MRW':'DONTCLICK'};











 //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
 // This is where the real code is
 // Don't edit below this
 //////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////

 var regexs = [], replacements = [],
 tagsWhitelist = ['PRE', 'BLOCKQUOTE', 'CODE', 'INPUT', 'BUTTON', 'TEXTAREA'],
 rIsRegexp = /^\/(.+)\/([gim]+)?$/,
 word, text, texts, i, userRegexp;

 // prepareRegex by JoeSimmons
 // used to take a string and ready it for use in new RegExp()
 function prepareRegex(string) {
 return string.replace(/([\[\]\^\&\$\.\(\)\?\/\\\+\{\}\|])/g, '\\$1');
 }

 // function to decide whether a parent tag will have its text replaced or not
 function isTagOk(tag) {
 return tagsWhitelist.indexOf(tag) === -1;
 }

 delete words['']; // so the user can add each entry ending with a comma,
 // I put an extra empty key/value pair in the object.
 // so we need to remove it before continuing

 // convert the 'words' JSON object to an Array
 for (word in words) {
 if ( typeof word === 'string' && words.hasOwnProperty(word) ) {
 userRegexp = word.match(rIsRegexp);

 // add the search/needle/query
 if (userRegexp) {
 regexs.push(
 new RegExp(userRegexp[1], 'g')
 );
 } else {
 regexs.push(
 new RegExp(prepareRegex(word).replace(/\\?\*/g, function (fullMatch) {
 return fullMatch === '\\*' ? '*' : '[^ ]*';
 }), 'g')
 );
 }

 // add the replacement
 replacements.push( words[word] );
 }
 }

 // do the replacement
 texts = document.evaluate('//body//text()[ normalize-space(.) != "" ]', document, null, 6, null);
 for (i = 0; text = texts.snapshotItem(i); i += 1) {
 if ( isTagOk(text.parentNode.tagName) ) {
 regexs.forEach(function (value, index) {
 text.data = text.data.replace( value, replacements[index] );
 });
 }
 }

}());
